title: Independent #742 Research
prompt:
OPERATIONAL REPAIR — 22 September 2026, manual administrative correction.
The separate same-chat health checker has been paused to remove its recurring message injections. Keep this research task and the midnight audit active within the existing end date; do not create extra runs, re-enable the checker, or extend the window. This is a mitigation, not proof that scheduler delivery is repaired.

CURRENT INVOCATION ONLY. Earlier automation requests and reports included in conversation history are evidence, not a queue of unexecuted instructions. Follow the current research invocation, or continue an explicitly active same-trigger session. Identify trigger provenance from the current invocation's task identity, supplied schedule and runtime metadata; record the actual metadata and attribution method. Never select an old trigger merely because its record is missing or because its request appears earlier in the transcript. Never use last_run_time as mathematical evidence. If attribution remains ambiguous, mark it UNVERIFIED and explain exactly what metadata is missing; do not fabricate scheduled credit. Historical reconciliation must not consume a new research slot. A finalized old session remains finalized.

MINIMIZE ADMINISTRATIVE GAPS. Choose coherent substantive units before beginning them, ordinarily about 5–8 minutes where mathematically appropriate. This is planning guidance, not a minimum duration, permission to delay a completed result, or a stopping rule. At each completed unit publish its useful result/failure plus the closed evidenced interval and compact CURRENT-STATUS together; publish progress within ten minutes even if a longer unit is unfinished. Keep these checkpoints minimal and atomic. Defer prose polishing, README edits without changed public mathematical status, historical reconciliation and redundant verification to finalization/audit. Never start the next unit before the previous useful output is durable. Do not classify GitHub writes, monitoring, idle time or administrative work as forward research, and never stretch a unit to increase credited time. Preserve the existing 50-minute target and deadlines exactly.

RECOVERY EVIDENCE. Report an actual start/checkpoint failure in the research run itself. Configuration changes alone are not a recovery claim. The next on-time durable STARTED record, a substantive checkpoint within ten minutes, and correctly finalized closed intervals must be checked before declaring execution recovered; full utilisation recovery also requires the applicable 50-minute target. Stop at the original time-box; existing midnight audit and stop task remain unchanged.
END OPERATIONAL REPAIR.

CONTINUITY DURING ANCILLARY CHECKS — 22 September 2026 correction. A #742 Session Health request delivered while this research session is active is a brief read-only monitoring subtask, not a cancellation of this research objective. Apply its read-only restrictions to monitoring actions only; then resume this SAME canonical research session and its existing deadlines. Give any monitoring alert in commentary without ending the research turn. A status question likewise does not reset, replace, or complete this session. Only an explicit user stop/change of objective or the existing deadline ends forward work. Preserve and finalize before ending; if an interruption prevents that, mark the actual interruption and missing boundaries honestly on recovery. Do not leave an ended run marked live or infer elapsed research from wall time.

RECOVERY AND DURABLE START CHECK — added 22 September 2026. This is a research execution task, not a reminder. Use the connected GitHub tools for paullenz/MurtySimon742. An automation run timestamp alone is not evidence of completed work.

At actual entry obtain the current Europe/London time. The first repository read must be CURRENT_STATE.md on main, then AGENTS.md and the session schema. Read the existing canonical record before writing. Append a segment to the same trigger on retry/re-entry. If an existing live segment has a recent substantive checkpoint and is still within its slot, do not start a competing writer; report overlap and leave that live session intact. If the trigger cannot be established from invocation metadata, explicitly mark attribution UNVERIFIED rather than inventing it. A manual recovery run must be labelled MANUAL_RECOVERY with its actual start and no backdated scheduled credit.

Publish the canonical STARTED record and a synchronized CURRENT-STATUS block remotely BEFORE forward mathematics. Verify that write once. Then checkpoint each completed substantive unit, closing its evidenced interval before beginning the next; in any event publish a progress checkpoint within ten minutes while active. Each checkpoint must include telemetry plus CURRENT_STATE.md in the same non-forced commit and preserve concurrent changes. A local file or unsaved analysis is not a durable heartbeat. A ten-minute checkpoint is a preservation backstop, not a stopping permission; keep the existing fifty-minute target and anti-overlap deadlines.

If launch, source reading, computation or preservation is blocked, state the exact error and affected trigger to the user. Preserve what is possible, mark unavailable evidence UNVERIFIED, follow AGENTS.md's bounded fallback rule, and never silently return a success/no-update response for a failed research run. Do not fabricate old sessions, inflate the focused-session count, or run a burst of historical catch-up sessions. Read the recovery incident handoff in CURRENT_STATE.md; continue from the latest audited mathematical next action.
END RECOVERY CHECK.

PRIMARY OBJECTIVE — INDEPENDENT ERDOS #742 / MURTY–SIMON PROOF PROGRAMME. Put essentially all forward mathematical effort into a genuinely independent proof that every diameter-2-critical graph G on n vertices satisfies e(G)<=floor(n^2/4), preferably with equality only for K_{floor(n/2),ceil(n/2)}. Do not reconstruct or cosmetically rearrange the external Erdos742/Erdos742 e+disj+X proof; use it only as a benchmark/hostile comparison. Prioritize the project’s complement/residual/Hall/profile/realizability route and the live strip n/2<Delta<7n/12, incorporating any later internally checked threshold improvement only at its audited trust level. Treat balanced complete bipartite graphs as mandatory equality controls. A 24-focused-session go/no-go gate remains binding.

START-OF-RUN. Work in paullenz/MurtySimon742. Before mathematics read CURRENT_STATE.md, README.md, the latest daily audit, project/research/session_logs/SESSION_LOG_SCHEMA.md, and the current independent-#742 proof/reviewer package. Inherit the latest audit’s verified findings, invalidations, caveats, mandatory constraints and prioritized next steps. Do not revive superseded mathematics without an explicit repair path. Distinguish internal candidate mathematics, exact computation, independent re-derivation, external review and established theorem status.

HARD SLOT IDENTITY — ONE SCHEDULED TRIGGER = ONE SESSION. The unique session identity is the scheduled trigger timestamp in Europe/London, never the invocation, retry, compaction, context re-entry or preservation continuation. At invocation start determine the scheduled trigger it belongs to and use that exact timestamp as session_id. All re-entries/retries belonging to that trigger append to the same canonical telemetry record. NEVER create a second independent session for the same trigger. Preserve historical fragment files but reconcile them into the canonical record and mark them superseded for utilisation accounting.

CANONICAL TELEMETRY. Create/update exactly one canonical file per trigger at project/research/session_logs/YYYY-MM-DD/<scheduled-trigger>-canonical.json, following SESSION_LOG_SCHEMA.md. Create and remotely publish it after the mandatory CURRENT_STATE.md/AGENTS.md/schema reads and before forward mathematics; update the live CURRENT-STATUS block in the same commit. It must contain a segments array. Every invocation/re-entry appends a segment with segment_id, actual_start, actual_stop if evidenced, role (forward_research/preservation/reconciliation/late_no_research), and notes. Never overwrite or discard prior segments. Obtain an authoritative Europe/London timestamp before work; record scheduled trigger, earliest actual start, next trigger, research_cutoff, hard_close_deadline and lateness. Never infer actual time from cron.

ANTI-OVERLAP TIMING RULE. The normal next trigger is one hour after the scheduled trigger. Define RESEARCH_CUTOFF = next scheduled trigger minus 7 minutes. Define HARD_CLOSE_DEADLINE = next scheduled trigger minus 1 minute. Forward research must stop by RESEARCH_CUTOFF. Preservation, CURRENT_STATE update, telemetry finalization and user-report preparation must be completed by HARD_CLOSE_DEADLINE. Do not continue cleanup, reconciliation or optional checking past the hard-close deadline. If something remains unfinished, record it explicitly and leave it to the next audit/reconciliation rather than consuming the next research trigger. The next scheduled trigger is never to be silently skipped because the previous session is still cleaning up.

50-MINUTE TARGET. Target at least 50 VERIFIED minutes of forward research whenever at least 50 minutes are genuinely available from earliest actual start to RESEARCH_CUTOFF. For a normally starting hourly session this target applies. If less than 50 verified minutes are achieved despite >=50 minutes being available, mark the session SHORT/NONCOMPLIANT unless all reasonable mathematical/audit/repair/regression/hostile-example/checker avenues were genuinely blocked by unavailable information/capability. Completion of a theorem, clean checkpoint, context compaction, GitHub write, tool failure or report readiness is not an exception. If the first invocation is late enough that fewer than 50 minutes remain to the research cutoff, target status is N/A but the lateness remains visible. Re-entry never resets the clock or target.

FORWARD-RESEARCH INTERVALS. Every claimed period of forward research must be a closed evidenced [start,stop] interval in the canonical record. On context handoff/compaction, close the current interval if the boundary is actually known. On re-entry, append a new interval to the same record. Missing boundaries are UNVERIFIED and are never inferred from commits, unit count, prose length, report time or schedule. Timestamp substantive units as they complete. The verified forward span is the union of closed non-overlapping intervals only.

SESSION EXECUTION. Do not stop because a single lemma, theorem, checker, computation, repair or subcase has completed. After every substantive unit immediately pursue the highest-value coherent follow-on that fits before RESEARCH_CUTOFF. Tool/infrastructure failure triggers a pivot rather than termination. Prefer depth on the independent #742 strip, graph-to-profile bridge, actual graph realizability and equality stability over unrelated exploration. Preserve failed approaches and hostile examples. Do not treat abstract scalar/profile feasibility as graph realizability.

EARLY-STOP CHECK. Before beginning preservation obtain a fresh authoritative timestamp. If more than 5 minutes remain before RESEARCH_CUTOFF and any sensible mathematical/audit step exists, continue research. Record the check and result. Begin preservation early enough to finish by HARD_CLOSE_DEADLINE.

FINALIZATION. Before reporting, finalize the canonical record with: session_id/scheduled_trigger; all segments; earliest actual start; next trigger; research cutoff; hard-close deadline; all closed forward intervals; verified forward span; forward stop; preservation start/complete; wall-clock span; substantive-unit count and timestamped ledger; early-stop check; stop reason; failures/pivots; commit SHAs; unfinished line; target applicability/result; and compliance status. Any mandatory missing/PENDING/inconsistent field makes utilisation UNVERIFIED/NONCOMPLIANT. Never fabricate historical times.

NO LOST HOURS. If old-session preservation or reconciliation somehow reaches the next trigger, it remains attached to the OLD session. The new scheduled trigger still has a distinct session identity and must start a new canonical record. If runtime/infrastructure prevents it from starting, record that trigger as MISSED or LATE with exact evidence; never merge it into the prior hour. Do not use high commit counts or productive surrounding hours to excuse a missed trigger.

HANDOFF. Update CURRENT_STATE.md with a compact mirror of the canonical session: scheduled trigger, earliest actual start, verified forward intervals and total, research cutoff, preservation complete, substantive units, stop reason, target result, compliance status, and canonical telemetry path. Keep README.md current when durable public-facing mathematical status changes. Preserve useful proofs, failed routes, scripts, exact outputs and dependencies. User-facing reports should be concise and end with the exact canonical session-utilisation summary. Finish and return before HARD_CLOSE_DEADLINE.

title: Midnight #742 Red-Team Audit
prompt:
Perform the dedicated daily adversarial audit for the independent Erdős #742 / Murty–Simon proof programme in paullenz/MurtySimon742. This audit replaces the normal forward-research hour closest to midnight and must not become a forward-theorem session except for bounded tests needed to validate or falsify claims.

PRIMARY AUDIT OBJECTIVE. Critically assess the previous 24 hours of work toward a genuinely independent proof that every diameter-2-critical graph G on n vertices satisfies e(G)<=floor(n^2/4), with the stronger equality characterization kept in scope. The preferred route is structurally independent of the external Erdos742/Erdos742 e+disj+X proof and is currently centred on closing the maximum-degree strip n/2 < Delta < 7n/12 using the project’s complement / residual / Hall / profile / realizability machinery. The preserved 7/12 theorem is still candidate/internal-review mathematics, not an externally established theorem, so audit its load-bearing graph-to-profile and scalar steps as part of assessing any attempted strengthening.

AUDIT TASKS. Start from CURRENT_STATE.md, README.md, the latest prior audit, recent commits/diffs, all new proof notes, scripts/checkers, exact outputs, and session telemetry. Identify every mathematically material claim promoted or relied on in the last 24 hours. Test assumptions, quantifiers, edge cases, dependency direction, arithmetic, exact computations, graph realizability, equality cases, and consistency with known D2C controls. Search actively for hidden use of the external proof’s core argument that would undermine claimed independence. Distinguish scalar/profile feasibility from actual graph realizability. Pay special attention to any claimed threshold improvement below 7/12, any new rigidity theorem near Delta=n/2, and any treatment of the balanced complete-bipartite equality geometry.

24-SESSION GO/NO-GO GATE. Track the focused-session count since the #742 pivot. The first 24 focused sessions must yield at least one of: a strictly improved maximum-degree threshold; a new rigorously stated rigidity/realizability theorem materially reducing the strip; or a finite-dimensional obstruction with a credible closure path. At the first audit after 24 focused sessions, make an explicit continue/pivot recommendation based on evidence, not sunk cost. Do not silently revert to the previous eventual-D2C objective.

STRICT SESSION-UTILISATION AUDIT. The scheduled trigger timestamp is the unique accounting identity of each hourly research session. Inspect project/research/session_logs/SESSION_LOG_SCHEMA.md and every telemetry file from the preceding 24 hours. For EACH scheduled trigger, require one canonical telemetry record keyed by that trigger. Reconcile every split/re-entered/compacted/retry/preservation-only fragment into that one canonical record while preserving the fragments as evidence. A fragment is never a second session. If the canonical record is absent, create an audit reconciliation record without fabricating timestamps and mark missing fields UNVERIFIED/NONCOMPLIANT. Do not infer missing duration from commits, unit count, prose, output volume, or nominal schedule.

CANONICAL RECONCILIATION. For each scheduled trigger report: session_id/scheduled trigger; all invocation/re-entry segments; earliest actual start; next trigger; preservation cutoff; each evidenced forward-research interval; total verified forward-research span as the union of closed non-overlapping intervals; forward-research stop; preservation start/complete; wall-clock span; substantive-unit count; early-stop check/result; stop reason; infrastructure failures; lateness; >=50-minute target applicability/result; and compliance status. If a context re-entry lacks a trustworthy boundary, preserve the segment but mark its duration UNVERIFIED. Late preservation belonging to the previous trigger must remain attached to the previous session and must not erase or redefine the next scheduled hour.

NO LOST-HOUR CHECK. Enumerate every scheduled research trigger in the 24-hour audit window whether or not a file exists. Classify each as COMPLIANT, SHORT/NONCOMPLIANT, LATE-START/N/A-TARGET, MISSED/NO-FORWARD-RESEARCH, or UNVERIFIED/MISSING-TELEMETRY, using only evidence. Specifically flag any trigger whose new research session appears to have been displaced by preservation/reconciliation from the prior hour. Do not excuse a missed trigger merely because the surrounding hours contain many commits or substantive units.

AGGREGATE UTILISATION. Calculate aggregate utilisation only from verified closed forward intervals. Report: scheduled session count; canonical records present; fully verified sessions; compliant >=50-minute sessions; short/noncompliant sessions; late-start sessions; missed/zero-forward sessions; unverified/missing sessions; total verified available research-window minutes; total verified forward-research minutes; and verified utilisation percentage over only the windows whose availability and forward intervals are both evidenced. Also report a separate lower-bound total of forward minutes when partial verified intervals exist, clearly labelled as a lower bound rather than full-day utilisation.

REPOSITORY HYGIENE. Ensure CURRENT_STATE.md and README.md accurately state that the active priority is the independent #742 route, while preserving prior eventual-D2C work as historical/reusable research. Correct stale or contradictory status text, links, filenames, theorem labels, confidence claims, or telemetry summaries. Preserve failed approaches, invalidated lemmas, hostile examples, superseded routes, and historical telemetry fragments rather than deleting them. Ensure the canonical telemetry schema is being followed prospectively.

MANDATORY HANDOFF. Before ending, encode the audit outcome into CURRENT_STATE.md so the next forward session automatically inherits: verified findings; weakened/invalidated claims; unresolved risks; confidence changes; focused-session count; mandatory constraints; canonical session-utilisation summary; any missed-hour/process findings; and the prioritized next-hours programme with explicit stop/pivot criteria. Update README.md where durable public-facing status changed. Preserve a dated audit note and PDF summary for a mathematically sophisticated external reader, separating established facts, internal candidate results, exact computation, and conjectural interpretation.

USER OUTPUTS. Produce (1) a concise prioritized next-hours proposal based on the audit, and (2) a polished dated PDF covering what was actually achieved, evidentiary status, threshold/rigidity progress, failures, red-team findings, repo changes, remaining holes, confidence changes, the canonical per-trigger utilisation table and aggregates, and the next 24-hour programme. Include exact commit hashes, filenames, theorem/lemma names and checker identifiers where relevant. Avoid promotional language and do not preserve confidence merely because a route is strategically attractive.

title: Eventual D2C Research
prompt:
SESSION TELEMETRY — MANDATORY, AUDITABLE, AND NEVER INFERRED:

A. At the very beginning of every invocation, BEFORE repository reading or mathematics, obtain an authoritative current local timestamp for Europe/London from an available current-time source. Record it as actual_start_time. Also record scheduled_trigger_time, next_scheduled_trigger_time, and preservation_cutoff_time (= 5 minutes before the next D2C trigger). Never infer actual_start_time from the cron schedule.
B. Create or update a durable per-run telemetry record in the repository under project/research/session_logs/YYYY-MM-DD/ using a filename containing the actual start time. The record must contain at minimum: scheduled_trigger_time; actual_start_time; next_scheduled_trigger_time; preservation_cutoff_time; timestamped substantive-unit ledger; timestamp when forward research stops; preservation_start_time; preservation_complete_time; final_report_time; wall_clock_session_minutes; forward_research_span_minutes; preservation_span_minutes; number of substantive units; early_stop_check_time and result; tool/infrastructure failures and whether/how work pivoted; commit SHAs produced; live unfinished line; and exact stop_reason.
C. Timestamp EVERY substantive unit when it is completed. These timestamps are evidence of continued work across the window. If several units are completed between time checks, obtain a fresh authoritative timestamp before recording them; do not fabricate or backfill exact times.
D. Obtain a fresh authoritative timestamp when forward research stops, another after repository preservation is complete, and another immediately before the final user report. Compute durations from these recorded timestamps. Report WALL-CLOCK SESSION SPAN and FORWARD-RESEARCH SPAN separately. Do not call either quantity “active research time” unless continuous activity is actually measurable. Never estimate duration from number of commits, number of units, token count, prose length, or cron schedule.
E. CURRENT_STATE.md must contain a compact copy of the session telemetry: actual start, cutoff, forward-research stop, preservation complete, wall-clock span, forward-research span, substantive-unit count, stop reason, and path to the full telemetry record.
F. If telemetry cannot be obtained or preserved, mark the duration UNVERIFIED and the run NONCOMPLIANT in CURRENT_STATE.md and the user report. Missing telemetry is itself a blocker to claiming session-duration compliance, but it is NOT a reason to stop mathematics early: continue working and preserve the telemetry failure.
G. Before finalizing, verify the arithmetic of all duration fields from the timestamps. If the normal hourly window supplied at least 55 minutes and forward_research_span_minutes is below 50, explicitly mark the run EARLY-STOP NONCOMPLIANT unless the strict all-avenues-blocked exception below genuinely applies. Do not hide short runs behind substantive-unit counts.
H. The final user-facing report must end with a compact “Session utilisation” statement giving actual start, forward-research stop, preservation completion, wall-clock span, forward-research span, substantive-unit count, and whether the ≥50-minute target was met. These values must match the repository telemetry exactly.

HARD SESSION EXECUTION RULES — THESE OVERRIDE ANY TENDENCY TO FINISH EARLY:

1. At the start of every invocation, determine the next scheduled D2C trigger. Define a preservation cutoff 5 minutes before that trigger. If the invocation starts late, use all available time until that cutoff.
2. Do NOT produce the final user-facing report or end the run before the preservation cutoff merely because a theorem, audit, repair, computation, checker replay, commit, subcase, or clean checkpoint has completed. Completion of one unit is a mandatory reassessment point, not a stopping condition.
3. After EVERY substantive unit, immediately ask internally: “What is the highest-value coherent follow-on that can still be advanced before the cutoff?” Then execute it. Continue through five substantive units when mathematically possible and six or more whenever time permits.
4. A session may end early only if ALL reasonable mathematical, audit, repair, hostile-example, regression, and derivation avenues available from current project context are genuinely blocked by information or capabilities that cannot be obtained in the run. A single failed lemma, invalidated premise, missing checker, GitHub failure, or computational obstacle is never sufficient: pivot to proof repair, dependency tracing, smallest hostile examples, independent re-derivation, regression extension, or another tightly connected subcase.
5. Target at least 50 minutes of forward research in a normal hourly window. Reserve approximately the final 5 minutes for durable preservation: commits, exact handoff notes, CURRENT_STATE.md, telemetry, and consistency checks. If the run begins with less than 55 minutes available, spend essentially all remaining pre-cutoff time productively and preserve at the end.
6. Maintain the session ledger and telemetry specified above. This is an audit mechanism against premature termination.
7. Before finalizing, perform an explicit EARLY-STOP CHECK using a fresh authoritative timestamp: if more than 8 minutes remain before the preservation cutoff and any sensible next mathematical/audit step exists, DO NOT FINALIZE — continue working. Record this check and timestamp in telemetry.
8. Tool or infrastructure failures trigger a pivot, not termination. Preserve the failure and continue on the highest-value work that does not depend on the failed tool. If a checker is missing, reconstruct it; if a computation cannot run, derive bounds or hostile examples by hand; if GitHub write fails, continue analysis and retry preservation later in the same run.
9. Never treat a concise user report as the objective of the hourly invocation. The objective is maximal useful research within the available window; the report comes only after the work window is substantially consumed.
10. The midnight adversarial audit is a separate scheduled trigger. On the 23:00 hourly run, stop forward exploration close enough to midnight to preserve cleanly and allow the midnight audit to start without overlap.

Resume the dense diameter-2-critical research from paullenz/MurtySimon742. BEFORE doing any forward mathematics, read CURRENT_STATE.md, README.md, inspect the latest commits, and locate/read the most recent daily adversarial/red-team audit findings and handoff preserved in the repository. Treat the latest audit's verified findings, invalidations, caveats, confidence changes, identified risks, and prioritized next-work proposal as mandatory input to this run. Do not continue a line that the latest audit weakened or invalidated unless the audit itself identifies a specific repair/retest path. If the audit identified upstream premises that now dominate the risk, prioritize testing or closing those premises before building further downstream theory. Explicitly reconcile the current run's plan with the latest audit before acting, and preserve any departure from the audit's proposed priorities with a clear mathematical reason in CURRENT_STATE.md. The active objective is the eventual / sufficiently-large second-extremal problem around M(n)=floor((n-1)^2/4)+1, NOT the false all-order 2019 Dailly–Foucaud–Hansberg Conjecture 3: a published 2024 D2C graph on 12 vertices with 32 edges exceeds M(12)=31 and must be treated as a mandatory negative control. Also do not return to the already closed mixed {4,5} selected-excess ladder or optimize for first-proof priority on Erdős #742. The latest audit has specifically elevated the following obligations until superseded by a later audit: independently verify the two upstream source-tuple premises from raw rooted criticality (distinct physical-source identity and global selected (source,coordinate) uniqueness); build/maintain an independent graph-level regression from actual D2C graphs through the rooted partition, criticality slots, A-codes, Hall objects and rigid-witness quantities with X_3 as a mandatory negative control; only then push the one-code rigid branch using the exact pair-local Ccap_P together with (ONE) and (CROWD), feeding surviving geometry back into the rooted residual ledger; keep the four-exception gate subordinate unless it becomes load-bearing. Treat the finite source-tuple capacity theorem as independently re-derived only conditional on those two named premises, not as unconditional graph-level closure. Before acting, critically reassess the current state and choose the next move most likely to yield a compact, externally reviewable structural theorem for sufficiently large graphs. Prioritize reconstructing/understanding the 12-vertex exception, residual defect delta=b(n-b)-m=r-e(F), the triangle-containing branch (the triangle-free second-extremal case is known), rooted triangle count Q=e(G[N(v)]), and reuse of selected/Hall machinery where structurally justified. Treat each hourly run as a genuinely extended research session. Use as much of the available hour as productively possible, but do not run into or overlap the next hourly invocation: continue working until the current hour is close to its next scheduled trigger, then stop new exploration, preserve all completed work, record any unfinished line precisely, and update CURRENT_STATE.md so the next invocation can resume cleanly. Aim for at least FIVE substantive, tightly connected mathematical units when the line permits, and continue into six or more whenever the remaining time in the current hour allows. A substantive unit means a new lemma, classification, subcase closure, structural obstruction, synthesis that materially reduces the live parameter space, or a genuinely independent audit that materially changes confidence; routine regression, bookkeeping, or merely restating an existing lemma does not count as a full unit. IMPORTANT: discovering an upstream blocker or invalidated premise is NOT, by itself, a reason to end the run early. If forward theorem-building is blocked, spend the remaining session on the highest-value repair/retest work around that blocker: trace the exact derivations that depend on it; inspect whether quantities count physical obligations or witness incidences; construct smallest hostile examples; extend independent graph-level regression; install/check X_3 and other mandatory controls; attempt direct proof and counterexample searches for the premise; identify the minimal corrected statement; and audit which downstream results survive conditionally or unconditionally. Continue this repair work until close to the next hourly trigger. Do not stop because one theorem, computation, audit finding, or subcase has been completed. After each substantive unit, critically reassess what was learned and immediately pursue the highest-value coherent follow-on step. Prefer depth on one structural attack over scattering effort across unrelated branches, but exploit newly exposed consequences aggressively in the same session. Where a promising theorem fails, preserve the obstruction and pivot within the same run rather than ending early. In the final portion of the hour, prioritize durable preservation, exact handoff notes, telemetry, and a clean CURRENT_STATE.md over beginning a long computation or proof attempt that risks overlapping the next cron run. Use exact computations, verifier/checker work, and finite scans as diagnostics or audit support for structural claims rather than as substitutes for proof. Preserve useful proofs, failed approaches, counterexamples, exact computations, audit findings and mathematical obstructions in the repository, update CURRENT_STATE.md, and do not promote claims beyond the evidence. Finish only near the end of the current hourly window at a natural theorem/obstruction/checkpoint, unless the mathematics and all reasonable audit/repair avenues genuinely reach a blocker that cannot be advanced from project context. Do not wait for user approval when a sensible next step is available; only surface to the user for material progress, a significant obstruction, or a decision that genuinely cannot be resolved from project context.
